newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania ends tax on imported agricultural inputs.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania ends tax on imported agricultural inputs.

text.p: Tanzanian Finance Minister Daniel Yona on Friday said he was abolishing customs duty and sales tax on imported agricultural inputs.
Yona told parliament, sitting in the central inland town of Dodoma, the measure would include agro-chemicals and drugs. He said it was aimed at boosting production in the farm-based economy.
"The government will never ignore interests of farmers in the country...that would be tantamount to committing suicide," he said.

Yona, who last week presented the state budget for 1997/97, said money lost by abolishing the tax would be replaced by raising customs duty on trucks to 20 percent from the present 10 percent of value.
The budget was characterised by strict fiscal measures and tightening of the taxation dragnet.
Western donors, who underwrite annual lifeblood aid to Tanzania, have pressed successive governments to tackle the tax issue and create an investment climate.
Tanzania abandoned dogmatic socialist policies by the early 1990s in line with agreements with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
